message.content:
The “best” film of 2020 is a matter of taste and criteria, but most critics and audiences agree that **“Parasite”** remains the standout movie of that year.

### Why “Parasite” tops the list

| Criterion | How “Parasite” excels |
|-----------|-----------------------|
| **Critical acclaim** | 8.6/10 on Rotten Tomatoes, 97% on Metacritic |
| **Awards** | Best Picture, Best Director, Best Original Screenplay, Best International Feature Film at the 92nd Academy Awards (awarded in 2020) |
| **Cultural impact** | Sparked global conversations about class, inequality, and the power of storytelling |
| **Storytelling & direction** | Bong Joon‑ho’s masterful blend of dark comedy, thriller, and social satire |
| **Box‑office** | Grossed $257 million worldwide despite pandemic‑related restrictions |

### Other notable contenders

| Film | Year Released | Highlights |
|------|---------------|------------|
| **“The Trial of the Chicago 7”** | 2020 | Powerful courtroom drama, strong ensemble cast, 8.1/10 RT |
| **“Soul”** | 2020 | Pixar’s heartfelt exploration of purpose, 8.2/10 RT |
| **“Tenet”** | 2020 | Christopher Nolan’s mind‑bending action, 7.5/10 RT |
| **“Nomadland”** | 2020 | Oscar‑winning Best Picture (awarded in 2021), 8.0/10 RT |

### Bottom line

If you’re looking for the film that captured the most critical praise, earned the highest accolades, and left a lasting cultural footprint, **“Parasite”** is the best movie of 2020. If you prefer a more recent release that still made waves in 2020, “The Trial of the Chicago 7” and “Soul” are excellent choices.
